attacks.claim: The public Recent signers panel renders full name and full postal code for every signer. This violates the agreed rule that public signer lists show at most first name, last initial and city, and it would be exposed from the first 10% canary hour.
The organizer-updates checkbox is pre-ticked. For EU signers, GDPR Art. 4(11) and Art. 7 require a clear affirmative act, so default-on marketing consent is not valid consent.

Validation errors are conveyed only by red border and background colour. The JS never writes text into the aria-live .form-error paragraph and sets no aria-invalid or aria-describedby, so screen-reader users get no explanation. This fails WCAG 1.4.1 and 3.3.1/3.3.3, which are agreed AA requirements.
attacks.evidence: for (const name of fields) form.elements[name].classList.add('is-invalid'); ...

attacks.claim: The submit handler handles only 422 and ok. A 409 duplicate, 500, or network failure gives the signer no feedback, and the button is not disabled during submit, so double-clicks produce silent 409s.
attacks.evidence: if (res.ok) window.location = res.headers.get('Location');  // no else branch; QA: Duplicate signature (same email) rejected with 409 | Pass

attacks.claim: The 409 duplicate response tells any caller whether a given email has already signed a specific petition, a membership-disclosure side channel on political-participation data.
attacks.evidence: Duplicate signature (same email) rejected with 409 | Pass

attacks.claim: The public unauthenticated POST /sign has no CSRF token, rate limit, CAPTCHA or bot control described. Scripts can create fake signatures and trigger confirmation emails to arbitrary addresses. The artifact does not show whether these exist server-side, so this must be confirmed.
attacks.evidence: <form class="sign-form" action="/p/{{ petition.slug }}/sign" method="post" novalidate> ABSENT: csrf field, rate limit or bot control

attacks.claim: Every accepted submission triggers a Postmark confirmation with no send quota, per-address or per-petition cap, or budget ceiling. Spend and email-bombing exposure are unbounded.
attacks.evidence: Confirmation emails go through Postmark; ABSENT: send quota, budget ceiling or per-IP/per-petition cap on confirmation sends

attacks.claim: The sign form gives no privacy notice, controller identity or lawful basis at the point of collection, which GDPR Art. 13 requires for EU signers.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: privacy notice or link in sign.html; form contains only full_name, email, postal_code and newsletter_opt_in

attacks.claim: Retention for confirmed signatures (name, email, postal code) is undefined and no erasure or access path for signers is described, so storage limitation and data-subject rights cannot be shown.
attacks.evidence: unconfirmed signatures are not counted and are purged after 7 days | ABSENT: retention period and erasure procedure for confirmed signatures

attacks.claim: EU residency is routed from postal code alone with no country field, so EU signers with ambiguous or non-EU-format codes may be misrouted to us-east-1, a restricted transfer. The Postmark transfer mechanism is also not stated beyond the DPA.
attacks.evidence: eu-central-1 for EU-resolved postal codes, us-east-1 otherwise | <input id="postal" name="postal_code" required autocomplete="postal-code"> (no country input)

attacks.claim: The panel renders {{ s.city }}, but the form never collects city, and the artifact does not say how city is derived from postal code or where it is stored, so the displayed location is undefined.
attacks.evidence: Form fields: full_name, email, postal_code only | {{ s.city }}

attacks.claim: Organizer CSV exports give organizers signer email and postal code for opted-in signers, with no stated purpose limitation, controller/processor allocation or unsubscribe handling for organizer mail.
attacks.evidence: Organizers can export signers who opted in to updates as CSV; export is rate-limited and audit-logged.

attacks.claim: The QA row 'Recent signers renders 20 most recent confirmed' is marked Pass without checking which fields render, and it conflicts with the masking rule the artifact says is met. The axe scan also cannot verify colour-only errors, focus after 422 or announcements, so the AA evidence is weak.
attacks.evidence: Recent signers renders 20 most recent confirmed | Pass; axe-core automated scan on sign page | 0 violations

attacks.claim: Rollback only flips the flag. It does not remove PII already stored, names and postal codes already rendered and CDN-cached in the public panel, CSVs already exported, or confirmation emails in flight, and no takedown or purge plan is defined.
attacks.evidence: Rollback: flip petitions_signing off; sign form is replaced by the existing 'Follow this petition' button. No schema changes in this release

attacks.claim: The 24h watch gates only submit error rate and bounce rate. It would not detect public PII exposure, purge-job failure or unexpected CSV export volume, and no alert owner is named.
attacks.evidence: Watch sign_submit_error_rate (< 0.5%) and confirmation email bounce rate (< 2%) for 24h.

attacks.claim: The load test covers only signature writes at 400/s. The read path (15s polling per open page and recent_signers on every render) is untested, and viewer traffic is the likely launch-day bottleneck.
attacks.evidence: Load: 400 signatures/s sustained for 10 min, p95 210ms | Signature counts update live (polling every 15s, cached at the CDN for 10s)

attacks.claim: All confirmation email, including EU signer addresses, depends on a single vendor (Postmark) with no documented fallback or exit path.
attacks.evidence: Confirmation emails go through Postmark; DPA countersigned 2026-09-14

attacks.claim: The masking rule exists only as an inline template expression with no model method or test, so the privacy constraint can regress silently.
